title: Elimination Sign Check
prompt: Use this to debug the sign mistake before it turns into a wrong final answer.

steps.title: Read the structure first
steps.content: In the system $$3x + 2y = 17$$ and $$x - 2y = 3$$, the $y$-coefficients are already opposites. That means **adding** the equations will eliminate $y$ right away.

steps.title: Add corresponding terms carefully
steps.content:
Add left side to left side and right side to right side:

$$(3x + 2y) + (x - 2y) = 17 + 3$$

So $$4x = 20$$ and $$x = 5$$.

steps.title: Spot the common trap
steps.content: A frequent mistake is changing $$x - 2y$$ into $$x + 2y$$ without multiplying the **entire** equation by $-1$. Never flip just one sign in elimination.

steps.title: Back-substitute and finish
steps.content:
Substitute $x = 5$ into $$x - 2y = 3$$:

$$5 - 2y = 3$$
$$-2y = -2$$
$$y = 1$$

So the solution is **$(5, 1)$**.

fallback.markdown: If coefficients are already opposites, add the equations directly. Only change signs when you multiply the **whole** equation by $-1$. For $$3x + 2y = 17$$ and $$x - 2y = 3$$, adding gives $$4x = 20$$, so $x = 5$, and then $y = 1$.
